title: Kale and Apple Slaw
subtitle: Massaged kale and grated apple slaw with a lemon tahini dressing
excerpt: Thinly shredded curly kale massaged until tender, with coarsely grated sharp apple, sunflower seeds and a lemon-tahini dressing. A hearty slaw that holds its texture for two days and gets better as it sits.
sourceNotes: Kale slaw became popular in British and American cooking from around 2010, driven by the rise of kale as a health food and the development of the massaging technique that softens raw kale leaves to make them palatable as a salad base. The combination with apple and a tahini-lemon dressing follows the health-food-cafe repertoire that popularised kale in this period.

recipe.batchNotes: Keeps for 2 days in the fridge. The kale softens further and the flavour deepens.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Best made at least 15 minutes ahead after massaging. The kale continues to soften.

content.text: Raw kale is tough and bitter; massaged kale is tender and mildly sweet. The massaging step is not optional. Add the lemon juice and a pinch of salt to the stripped kale leaves and work them firmly with your hands for 2 to 3 minutes until the leaves feel soft and have reduced in volume by half. This breaks down the cell walls and removes most of the bitterness. The kale can now be dressed and left; it only improves.

items.prepNote: stalks removed, leaves very finely shredded
cored and coarsely grated, skin on

content.text: Strip the kale leaves from the stalks and shred finely. Put in a large bowl with a generous pinch of salt and half the lemon juice. Massage firmly with your hands for 2 to 3 minutes until the leaves have darkened, wilted and feel tender and silky rather than stiff. The volume will reduce noticeably.
Make the dressing and dress the slaw

Whisk together {{tahini}} of tahini, the remaining lemon juice, {{olive-oil}} of olive oil, {{honey}} of honey, {{sea-salt-fine}} of salt and {{black-pepper}} of pepper. Add cold water a teaspoon at a time until the dressing is pourable. Pour over the kale and toss. Add the grated apple, red onion and {{sunflower-seeds}} of toasted sunflower seeds and toss again. Leave for 15 minutes before serving.

items.symptom: Kale is still tough and bitter
items.cause: Not massaged long enough, or stalks left in.
items.fix: Remove every bit of stalk before massaging; the stalks are too tough to eat raw. Massage for a full 3 minutes, not 30 seconds. The leaves should feel noticeably different in your hands before you stop.
Toss the grated apple immediately with the lemon juice in the bowl. The acid prevents browning.

content.text: Kale slaw arrived with the kale trend of the 2010s, emerging from health cafes and salad bars. The massaging technique was the key discovery that made raw kale practical for salads: without it, kale is too tough and bitter to eat comfortably. With it, the leaf becomes one of the most robust and long-lasting salad bases available. This slaw is at its best in autumn when kale is sweetest and cooking apples are in season.
